docs.title: Multi-Agent AI Studio Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for Multi-Agent AI Studio.

Use this portal to understand architecture, implementation decisions, operational guidance, and learning pathways for local agentic AI systems.

docs.title: API Contract Notes
docs.text:
• Authenticated endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
  • Token rotation supported through POST /api/v1/auth/refresh.
  • Destructive tool endpoints require X-Confirm-Token: CONFIRM-<ENV>.
  • Rate limiting is enforced per-scope via Redis-backed counters.
  • Workflow payloads must satisfy WorkflowSpec JSON schema.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Multi-Agent AI Studio provides an integrated environment to design, execute, monitor, and evaluate local-first agentic AI workflows.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Most agent tools optimize either experimentation or production operations. This platform bridges both: engineering velocity and operational rigor with privacy-first local execution.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• Frontend (Next.js) renders product surfaces for chat, workflows, memory, evaluation, and monitoring.
  • Backend (FastAPI) hosts REST + SSE APIs, orchestration services, model routing, and persistence.
  • Supervisor runtime (LangGraph) coordinates planner, executor, reviewer, and critic stages.
  • Worker layer (ARQ) executes asynchronous jobs for long-running tasks.
  • Data stores:
  • PostgreSQL: transactional metadata.
  • Qdrant: vector retrieval.
  • Redis: queues and caching.
  • MinIO: object storage.
  • Observability via OpenTelemetry + Langfuse.

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Modular monolith backend for lower ops overhead while keeping domain isolation.
  • Versioned workflow DSL to make graph execution deterministic and auditable.
  • Capability-based model router to avoid brittle hardcoded model names.
  • Confirmation-gated destructive tools for safe local automation.

docs.title: Alternative Implementations
docs.text:
• Full microservices: stronger isolation, higher complexity.
  • Fixed model mapping: simpler, less adaptive.
  • No worker queue: easier setup, weaker reliability for heavy workloads.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep agent prompts and tool permissions minimal per role.
  • Track run/evaluation regressions before changing model-routing weights.
  • Keep workflow specs versioned and backward-compatible.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Defines role-specific agent behavior, tools, memory scopes, and model policies.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Specialized agents improve reliability by narrowing scope and permissions.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• Agent definitions persisted in agents table.
  • Workflow compiler binds agents to orchestration graph.
  • Supervisor dispatches based on workflow + task context.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Use least-privilege tool access.
  • Pair each agent with explicit reviewer criteria.
  • Track eval performance by agent role.

docs.title: Learning Path
docs.text:
1. Start API and web UI locally.
  2. Register account and create first workflow graph.
  3. Run chat orchestration and inspect model routing snapshot.
  4. Add memory records and query them.
  5. Ingest documents and test retrieval.
  6. Execute tool calls with confirmation headers.
  7. Run evaluation entries and cost estimation.
  8. Inspect traces and system metrics.

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text: This sequence builds practical understanding of modern agentic AI stack components: orchestration, retrieval, observability, and safety controls.

docs.title: Folder Structure
docs.text:
• apps/api: backend domains, API, orchestration, services.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Detects GPU availability and reports VRAM utilization for model scheduling.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text: GpuMonitor uses nvidia-smi --query-gpu and returns None on failure for graceful CPU fallback.

docs.title: 8GB VRAM Strategy
docs.text:
• Avoid loading many >6B models concurrently.
  • Prioritize smaller route-appropriate models.
  • Monitor free VRAM before spawning parallel heavy jobs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Linux with Docker and Docker Compose.
  • Python 3.12.10 available through uv.
  • Node.js 24+.
  • Ollama installed locally.
  • Optional GPU runtime (nvidia-smi) for accelerated inference.

docs.title: Backend Setup
docs.text:
cd /home/ahmad/AI/multi-agent-ai-studio
cp .env.example .env
make setup
make run-api

make setup now includes alembic upgrade head to ensure schema revision matches runtime.

docs.title: Frontend Setup
docs.text:
cd /home/ahmad/AI/multi-agent-ai-studio/apps/web
npm install
npm run dev

docs.title: Full Stack via Docker
docs.text:
cd /home/ahmad/AI/multi-agent-ai-studio
docker compose up -d --build

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: LangGraph runs deterministic orchestration for supervisor-led multi-agent execution.

docs.title: Why It Exists
docs.text: Graph orchestration enables explicit retries, validation checkpoints, and visibility into agent transitions.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
SupervisorRuntime builds a graph with nodes:

  1. Planner
  2. Executor
  3. Reviewer
  4. Critic

Each node selects model dynamically via ModelRouter, executes task prompt, and enriches state.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep state small and explicit.
  • Separate planning and critique prompts.
  • Log model and latency metadata per node.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Stores multi-layer memory records for continuity and context reuse.

docs.title: Memory Types
docs.text:
• short_term
  • long_term
  • semantic
  • episodic
  • conversation
  • project
  • agent

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
• Create memory entry with salience + TTL.
  • Query by owner with optional scope + memory_type.
  • Get/update/delete specific records.
  • Summarize memory slices via POST /api/v1/memory/summary.
  • Forget by policy via POST /api/v1/memory/forget.
  • Periodic TTL pruning for expired records.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep high salience for durable preferences/facts.
  • Apply short TTLs to volatile run details.
  • Review memory drift periodically.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Provides execution visibility across chat/runs, system telemetry, and evaluation quality.

docs.title: Runtime Signals
docs.text:
• Trace records with span timeline (planner, executor, reviewer, critic).
  • Run linkage (run_id, status, output payload, model usage).
  • Host telemetry snapshots persisted to system_metrics.
  • GPU utilization and VRAM usage time-series.
  • Evaluation aggregates and history.

docs.text:

  • GET /api/v1/traces/{trace_id}

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
Frontend pages wired to live API data:

  • Dashboard: active runs, average stage latency, GPU/VRAM charts, eval score.
  • System Monitoring: health + telemetry table/time-series.
  • Evaluation: aggregate metrics + historical runs.
  • Traces: trace list + drill-down timeline.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep METRICS_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_SECONDS between 3 and 10 seconds.
  • Track rising VRAM + queue latency before increasing parallelism.
  • Use trace drill-down to isolate slow stages and routing misses.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Runs local language, OCR, embedding, and translation models used by routing and orchestration.

docs.title: Runtime Notes
docs.text:
• API endpoint default: http://localhost:11434.
  • Model router discovers capabilities from Ollama metadata.
  • No model names hardcoded in routing logic.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep at least one embedding-capable model available.
  • Prefer 2B-4B models for concurrent workflows on 8GB VRAM.
  • Warm key models before heavy runs.

docs.title: Optimization Levers
docs.text:
• Tune model-router scoring weights by latency and quality telemetry.
  • Limit concurrent heavy runs through queue backpressure.
  • Use chunk size/overlap tuned for retrieval quality vs throughput.
  • Keep database indices current for run/memory/document lookups.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
• API latency percentiles.
  • Queue depth and processing rate.
  • GPU VRAM usage and OOM events.
  • Retrieval latency and hit quality.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
Implements production-grade retrieval-augmented generation for local-first workflows:

  • Document registration and ingestion.
  • Embeddings via Ollama router-selected embedding model.
  • Vector storage in Qdrant.
  • Hybrid retrieval (semantic + keyword).
  • Embedding-based reranking.
  • Highlight snippets and source metadata for citation-ready responses.

docs.title: File Upload Connector
docs.text:
Route: POST /api/v1/rag/documents/{document_id}/ingest

Supported formats:

  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • Markdown / TXT
  • HTML
  • CSV
  • XLSX

docs.title: GitHub Connector
docs.text:
Route: POST /api/v1/rag/connectors/ingest

Payload:

  • connector: "github"
  • source_uri: repository clone URL
  • options: branch, max_files, max_file_bytes

Behavior:

  1. Shallow clone repository.
  2. Read allowed text/code files.
  3. Chunk + embed + index in Qdrant.

docs.title: Web Crawler Connector
docs.text:
Route: POST /api/v1/rag/connectors/ingest

Payload:

  • connector: "web"
  • source_uri: seed URL
  • options: max_pages, max_depth, same_domain

Behavior:

  1. Crawl pages breadth-first.
  2. Extract cleaned text with Trafilatura/BeautifulSoup.
  3. Chunk + embed + index.

docs.title: Retrieval Modes
docs.text:
Route: POST /api/v1/rag/retrieve

  • mode: semantic - vector similarity only.
  • mode: keyword - lexical scoring only.
  • mode: hybrid - weighted vector + lexical blend.

rerank: true applies secondary embedding similarity rerank on the top candidate pool.

docs.title: Recommended Defaults
docs.text:
• mode: "hybrid"
  • candidate_pool: 30
  • top_k: 5
  • rerank: true

docs.title: Operational Notes
docs.text:
• Keep connector metadata consistent for reliable filtering.
  • Limit crawler depth/pages for low-latency ingestion.
  • Prefer repository subsets for large monorepos.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text: Provides plugin-style tool execution for filesystem, terminal, and Python operations with confirmation, RBAC, audit logs, and rate limiting.

docs.title: Safety Model
docs.text:
• Tool manifests define destructive and confirmation requirements.
  • Destructive tools require X-Confirm-Token.
  • Filesystem operations constrained to /home/ahmad/AI.
  • Unsafe shell patterns blocked.
  • Terminal/Python execution has timeout guards.
  • Terminal/Python prefer container-isolated execution (TOOL_EXECUTION_MODE=container_preferred) and fall back to host with audit-visible stderr marker.
  • Destructive tool invocations are written to audit_logs.
  • Tool endpoints are scope rate-limited through Redis.

docs.title: Built-in Tool Endpoints
docs.text:
• POST /api/v1/tools/execute (manifest-based unified executor)
  • filesystem.read
  • filesystem.list
  • filesystem.search
  • filesystem.write
  • filesystem.move
  • filesystem.copy
  • filesystem.delete
  • terminal.exec
  • python.exec

docs.title: How To Add Custom Tool
docs.text:
1. Create a manifest with schema and safety flags.
  2. Register manifest in state._register_builtin_tools or plugin loader.
  3. Implement execution handler in router/service layer.

docs.title: Local Production-Like Deployment
docs.text:
1. Configure .env with secrets and service endpoints.
  2. Start dependencies via Docker Compose.
  3. Run DB migrations.
  4. Start API and worker processes.
  5. Start frontend service.
  6. Validate health endpoints and core user journeys.

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text:
• Auth login + token refresh path.
  • Agent/workflow CRUD.
  • Supervisor chat run.
  • RAG ingest and retrieval.
  • Tool execution with confirmation.
  • Evaluation write/read.
  • Trace and system metrics visibility.

docs.title: Core Stack (API + Worker + Ollama + Data Services)
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --build

This brings up:

  • api (FastAPI)
  • worker (ARQ background jobs)
  • ollama (local model runtime)
  • postgres, redis, qdrant, minio

docs.title: Guaranteed Ollama Connectivity
docs.text:
Compose wiring guarantees API/worker startup after Ollama health check:

  • api and worker depend on ollama: service_healthy
  • API startup fails fast if Ollama is unreachable or has no discoverable models
  • OLLAMA_BASE_URL defaults to http://ollama:11434 for container networking

docs.title: Optional Model Bootstrap
docs.text:
Pull configured Ollama models after stack starts:

docker compose --profile ollama-bootstrap up -d ollama-bootstrap

Configure model list via OLLAMA_BOOTSTRAP_MODELS in .env.

docs.title: Optional Langfuse Profile
docs.text: docker compose --profile observability up -d

docs.title: Stop and Clean Volumes
docs.text: docker compose down -v

docs.title: Is this cloud-dependent?
docs.text: No. Primary runtime is local Ollama.

docs.title: Can I add external providers later?
docs.text: Yes. Runtime uses adapter-friendly service boundaries.

docs.title: Why ARQ over Celery?
docs.text: Async-native integration with FastAPI and lighter local operations.

docs.title: Does it support multi-user?
docs.text: Schema and RBAC model are ready; current release is single-owner local-first.

docs.title: API cannot reach Ollama
docs.text:
• Check OLLAMA_BASE_URL in .env.
  • Verify curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags.

docs.title: GPU not detected
docs.text:
• Run nvidia-smi manually.
  • Confirm NVIDIA driver loaded in host and Docker runtime.

docs.title: Qdrant retrieval empty
docs.text:
• Ensure ingestion completed.
  • Validate embedding model availability and vector dimensions.

docs.title: Unauthorized API errors
docs.text:
• Confirm Authorization: Bearer <token> header.
  • Re-login to refresh expired token.
